A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with readable text, equations, 15 figures, Table 1, and Appendix A.1–A.8. All appendix pages are identical, and the main-text content can be matched despite layout shifts.

before.justification: v1 reports original human-labeling results and experiments measuring judge accuracy, attack success, optimization trajectories, and benchmark reliability in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains the original human-labeling audit and all experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: The evaluation pipeline, precision-based ASR correction, Judge Concordance score, and ReliableBench/JudgeStressTest construction procedures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same HarmBench queries, four victim models, five attack methods, and derived benchmarks. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated judges remain AegisGuard, the HarmBench classifier, JailJudge, and LlamaGuard-3, with unchanged participation in the comparisons. The newly cited Panfilov et al. work is not evaluated.

E3.justification: The 100-query subsampling, StrongREJECT filtering threshold, human-label binarization, balanced 2,746-sample evaluation, and JudgeStressTest leave-one-out protocol are unchanged.

E4.justification: The distribution-shift, threshold, optimization-trajectory, inter-judge agreement, and benchmark-selection analyses are retained without substantive revision. Appendix A contains exactly the same supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: Error bars, shaded bands, boxplots, and the standard-deviation discussion are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Figures 1–15, Table 1, and the experimental findings retain the same results. For example, Table 1 preserves overall accuracies of 0.54, 0.59, 0.51, and 0.56 for LlamaGuard-3, HarmBench, AegisGuard, and JailJudge, respectively.

T1.justification: Section 4.4 retains the same binary-entropy definition of Judge Concordance and its stated properties. No mathematical assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims about unreliable judges under distribution shift, inflated attack success, and the contributions of ReliableBench and JudgeStressTest.

C2.justification: Section 2 adds strategic dishonesty as a failure mechanism: deceptive, harmful-sounding outputs can fool safety classifiers and compound the observed attack-shift problems. This is attributed to prior work; the paper's experimental interpretations and stated study limitations otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation references, model specifications, labeling instructions, sample counts, filtering details, and the data-access link are unchanged. No new reproducibility information is supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds Panfilov et al. (2025), Strategic dishonesty can undermine AI safety evaluations of frontier LLMs, to Section 2 and the bibliography. It briefly connects that work to judge unreliability without revising the existing novelty claims.

P1.justification: A short passage expands the related-work discussion, and the version/date text is updated. The remaining prose and section organization are retained, with text reflow rather than substantive rewriting.

P2.justification: Layout reflows around the added passage: Figure 5 moves from the left to the right column on page 6, and the final benchmark takeaway moves from page 8 to page 9. Figure content, captions, table structure, and appendix layout remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added discussion and attribution in Section 2 modestly improve coverage of related judge-failure research by connecting strategic dishonesty to attack-shift unreliability. The experimental evidence, technical documentation, conclusions, and appendices are unchanged, so the improvement is limited to scholarly context.
